patients.summary: Young woman on her family's ranch in Hatfield who joins the practice at 20, is diagnosed with lupus in 2021 and hereditary angioedema the same fall, then has cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia, a class IV lupus nephritis admission with an airway attack, an angioedema ED visit and, in 2026, bubonic plague from a flea bite during ranch work near Flagstaff.

documents.body: Caller: Sonia Soto, 20. Turning 20 this summer and her pediatrician asked her to find an adult doctor. Insurance is through her dad's plan. Would like a new patient visit; prefers mornings because she works afternoons at a vet clinic. Booked 8/13 9:00 with Dr. Records release form emailed for the pediatric office.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20 y/o woman here to set up adult care; aged out of her pediatric practice.

No ongoing health problems. Takes no medicines, no supplements. NKDA.

OB/GYN: G1P0. Miscarriage at about 10 weeks in spring 2018, seen at an outside OB office, passed on its own, no D&C. Not sexually active since then and not planning to be right now. Periods regular.

PMH otherwise none. No surgeries, no hospital stays.

Family: Father has hereditary angioedema, diagnosed years ago with low C1 inhibitor; she has seen him need ER care for swelling. Paternal grandmother had 'swelling spells' that nobody ever named. Mother has lupus and an underactive thyroid. A maternal aunt has rheumatoid arthritis.

Social: Lives with her parents on the family ranch here in Hatfield - horses and some beef cattle. Works afternoons as a vet tech at a small-animal and equine clinic, taking classes toward her certification. Never smoked, no vaping, no alcohol, no drugs. Drives. Seat belt always.

ROS: negative. No rashes, joint pain, swelling, mouth sores, fevers or weight change.

Exam: Well-appearing. Vitals reviewed. HEENT normal, no oral lesions. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Joints without swelling or tenderness. Skin clear. Neuro grossly normal. Mood and affect good. PHQ-2 0.

A/P: Healthy young adult establishing care.
- Baseline CBC and CMP today.
- HIV and hep C screening once, she agrees.
- Declined STI testing; not sexually active.
- Pediatric records requested for vaccines; thinks she is up to date including HPV.
- Flu shot in the fall.
- Talked about her family history: told her to call us if she ever has swelling of the face, tongue, throat or belly pain episodes, given dad's HAE.
- Annual physical next summer.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sonia, everything from Tuesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests normal, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. Nice meeting you.

Immunizations abstracted: childhood series complete per their record (DTaP, IPV, Hib, hep B x3, MMR x2, varicella x2, hep A x2). Tdap and MenACWY 7/2010, HPV x3 2011-2012, MenACWY booster 8/2015. Growth charts and well visits otherwise unremarkable. No chronic diagnoses on their problem list.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 6 weeks of aching, stiff, puffy fingers and knuckles both hands, worst in the morning. Tired out by midday. For 2-3 weeks a red rash over the cheeks that flares badly after time outdoors at the ranch, plus a few painless mouth sores. No fevers she has measured. No chest pain, no SOB. No swelling episodes. No new meds or supplements. Mom has SLE.

O: Vitals reviewed. Erythematous rash over both malar areas and the nasal bridge, sparing the nasolabial folds. Two shallow ulcers on the hard palate. MCPs and PIPs of both hands swollen and tender, grip a little weak from pain. Wrists, elbows, knees without effusion. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.

A/P: Inflammatory polyarthritis with photosensitive malar rash and oral ulcers in a young woman whose mother has lupus - SLE is high on the list.
- CBC, CMP, UA today.
- Dermatology: their group has an opening at the end of the month and can biopsy/serologies if needed; sent the referral with the photos.
- Rheumatology referral placed too; their wait is several weeks.
- Sunscreen SPF 50, hat, long sleeves outdoors.
- Acetaminophen for pain is fine; holding off on prednisone until she is seen.
- She'll message if new symptoms - chest pain on breathing, swelling, dark urine.

documents.title: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sonia - your white count is a little low (3.4) and you're mildly anemic (hemoglobin 11.2). Kidney and liver tests and the urine were normal. These fit with what we talked about and dermatology and rheumatology will build on them. Your derm appointment is 6/29.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Lungs are clear. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size and mediastinal contours are normal. Osseous structures unremarkable.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 06/29/2021
Re: Sonia Soto, DOB 06/06/1999

Thank you for sending this 22-year-old veterinary technician with a sun-triggered facial eruption. She describes the rash coming up within a day of sun exposure, along with recurrent mouth sores, morning hand pain and fatigue over the past six weeks. She is not sexually active. No medications. NKDA.

Family history notable for lupus in her mother and hereditary angioedema in her father.

Exam: Fixed erythematous plaques across both malar eminences and the nasal bridge, nasolabial folds spared, no scarring or follicular plugging. Shallow ulcers of the hard palate. Swollen, tender MCP and PIP joints bilaterally. Scalp without alopecia.

Studies (drawn here 6/29, resulted 7/2): ANA positive at 1:640, homogeneous. Anti-dsDNA 186 IU/mL. Anti-Smith positive. C3 low at 64 mg/dL. ESR 48. aPTT prolonged at 41 seconds. VDRL reactive 1:2, which with no sexual exposure we suspect is a biologic false positive - would confirm with a treponemal test. Your CBC of 6/10 showed mild leukopenia and anemia. Chest radiograph clear.

Impression: Systemic lupus erythematosus with acute cutaneous lupus (malar rash), oral ulcers and inflammatory arthritis. Biopsy not needed given the serologies.

Plan: Broad-spectrum SPF 50+ daily, reapply outdoors, wide-brim hat and UPF clothing for ranch work. Systemic management to rheumatology - glad to see your referral is already in. We will see her back as needed for skin.

Dermatology

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily
Take 4 tablets daily for 2 weeks, then 3 daily for 2 weeks, then 2 daily for 2 weeks, then 1 tablet daily
Take 1 capsule (2000 IU) by mouth daily

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY CONSULTATION
Visit 7/27/2021

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Soto, 22, for newly diagnosed SLE. Since your referral the rash has eased with strict sun avoidance, but she still has 45 minutes of morning hand stiffness, fatigue and occasional mouth sores. No pleuritic pain, no Raynaud symptoms, no hair loss, no foamy urine. Not sexually active since a miscarriage at 10 weeks in 2018.

Exam: Faint residual malar erythema. Synovitis of MCPs 2-3 bilaterally and several PIPs. No effusions elsewhere. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.

Data: dermatology serologies reviewed (ANA 1:640, dsDNA 186, Smith positive, C3 64, ESR 48, aPTT 41, VDRL 1:2). Your 6/10 CBC with WBC 3.4 and Hgb 11.2, UA negative. Treponemal antibody drawn here today is nonreactive, so the VDRL is a biologic false positive.

Assessment: SLE - mucocutaneous and articular disease, mild leukopenia and anemia, low complement, no renal involvement on her urinalysis.

Plan:
1. Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily. Needs a baseline retinal exam this year.
2. Prednisone 20 mg daily, stepping down by 5 mg every 2 weeks to 5 mg daily, which she will stay on for now.
3. Vitamin D3 2000 IU daily while on steroids.
4. Labs every 3-6 months: CBC, CMP, UA, C3, dsDNA, ESR. Happy for these to be drawn at your office.
5. Pregnancy should be planned with us; she has no plans.
Follow-up in about 4 months, sooner if needed.

Rheumatology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. New SLE since last year - seen derm 6/29 and rheum 7/27 (letters in chart). On HCQ 200 bid, prednisone taper (now 15 mg, heading to 5), vit D 2000 IU. Joints much better, rash fading. Tolerating meds.

New today: when I asked about swelling she told me she's had maybe 4 or 5 episodes since last year - one hand or a foot blows up for 2-3 days, once her upper lip, no itching, no hives, no trouble breathing, goes away by itself. She didn't mention it before because 'it's just what Dad gets.' Never treated.

Meds as above. NKDA. Not sexually active. Never smoker, no ETOH. Working full days at the clinic again.

Exam: Well. Faint malar erythema only. No oral ulcers. Mild MCP tenderness L 2nd, no synovitis. No angioedema now. Heart, lungs normal. Abd soft. No edema.
PHQ-9 3.

A/P:
1. SLE - per rheum; on track with taper. Labs through us before her next rheum visit.
2. Recurrent non-pruritic swelling with father with C1-INH deficiency: needs an HAE evaluation - referred to allergy/immunology. If swelling ever involves the tongue or throat, call 911.
3. HCQ - ophthalmology referral for baseline retinal exam.
4. HM: Pap 2020 normal. Tdap 2020. COVID x2. Flu this fall. On prednisone - would avoid live vaccines going forward.
RTC 1 yr / prn.

documents.title: Allergy and Immunology Consultation
documents.author: allergy and immunology
documents.body:
ALLERGY & IMMUNOLOGY - NEW PATIENT
Seen 9/23/2021

Reason for referral: recurrent swelling; father with C1 inhibitor deficiency.

History: Since 2020 she has had several episodes of firm, non-itchy swelling of a hand, a foot and once the upper lip, each building over a day and fading over 2-3 days without treatment. No urticaria with any episode. No airway involvement so far, no abdominal attacks she can recall. No ACE inhibitor or estrogen exposure. Separately, she arrives today in the fourth day of a lupus flare: diffuse joint aching and her facial rash is back. SLE diagnosed 6/2021, on hydroxychloroquine 200 mg bid, prednisone 5 mg daily (taper finished earlier this month), vitamin D. NKDA.

Family: father HAE (C1-INH deficiency); paternal grandmother with unexplained swelling.

Exam: Erythematous rash spread fairly evenly over both cheeks and across the nasal bridge. No angioedema today. Oropharynx clear. Lungs clear. Hand joints tender without much swelling.

CBC today: platelets 100 K/uL, WBC 3.6, Hgb 11.4.

Impression: Clinical picture and family history strongly suggest hereditary angioedema. C4, C1 inhibitor antigen and function sent; will write with results. Platelets newly low - likely lupus-related; copying rheumatology.

Until results: avoid estrogen-containing contraception and ACE inhibitors; ED for any throat or tongue swelling.

Allergy & Immunology

documents.title: Allergy and Immunology - results and plan
documents.author: allergy and immunology
documents.body:
ALLERGY & IMMUNOLOGY - RESULTS LETTER

Re: Sonia Soto. Labs from 9/23/2021: C4 6 mg/dL (10-40), C1 esterase inhibitor antigen 7 mg/dL (21-39), C1 inhibitor function 24% (normal >67%).

Low antigen with low function confirms hereditary angioedema type I, consistent with her father's diagnosis.

Plan discussed with her by phone 10/4: start danazol 200 mg three times daily for long-term prophylaxis; prescription sent. Liver tests and lipids every 6 months on danazol. Danazol must not be taken in pregnancy - she understands and is not sexually active. Swelling of the tongue, throat or voice change: call 911. We will see her in about 6 months.

Allergy & Immunology

documents.title: Office Visit - fatigue, dark urine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: 2 wks fatigue, DOE, dizziness, dark urine.

HPI: 22F with SLE (HCQ, pred 5) and HAE type I (danazol). Gradual over 2 weeks: tired, short of breath on the walk up from the barn, lightheaded at work yesterday. Dark tea-colored urine, mostly first thing in the morning. Joints achy again and sun bothering her skin more. Has felt feverish on and off but never above 100. No bleeding, normal periods, no melena. No new meds, no NSAIDs, no recent illness. It's been a cold, wet March and she's been out feeding stock early mornings.

Exam: Pale conjunctivae. HR 104 regular. No scleral icterus I can see. No lymphadenopathy. No splenomegaly appreciated. Lungs clear. Mild MCP tenderness. No rash today. No edema.

Labs back at 12:40: Hgb 8.1 (11.2 last summer, 12.0 in Nov). Bili 2.4. Creatinine normal.

A/P: Acute anemia with dark urine and raised bilirubin in SLE - hemolysis until proven otherwise.
- Spoke with hematology on call; they will see her Tuesday 3/29 and do the hemolysis work-up there.
- Rheumatology notified.
- Strict ED precautions reviewed: syncope, chest pain, breathless at rest, worsening jaundice.
- Note off work through Monday. Stay warm.

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY CONSULTATION - 3/29/2022

Thank you for the urgent referral of Ms. Soto, 22, with SLE (6/2021) and HAE type I (10/2021).

HPI: Over two weeks, increasing tiredness, breathlessness on exertion, lightheadedness and dark urine. She also notes her joints aching again and her skin reacting to sun more than usual, with intermittent low-grade temperatures. She has not had a recent infection and takes no NSAIDs. Much of her work this month has been outdoors in cold, wet weather.
Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg bid, prednisone 5 mg, danazol 200 mg tid, vitamin D3 2000 IU. NKDA.

Exam: Pale; pulse 102. No jaundice. No lymph nodes palpable. Spleen not felt. Lungs clear.

Labs today: hemoglobin 7.9 g/dL, reticulocytes 8%, LDH 486 U/L, haptoglobin <10 mg/dL, total bilirubin 2.6 with direct 0.4 (indirect predominant). Spherocytes on the smear. Direct antiglobulin test positive for C3d, negative for IgG. Cold agglutinin titer 1:512.

Impression: Complement-mediated (cold) autoimmune hemolytic anemia, secondary to her lupus. Compensating marrow.

Plan:
- Folic acid 1 mg daily.
- Cold avoidance is the main treatment: warm layers, insulated gloves and a hat for barn work, no cold drinks, warm the car before driving. If she ever needs a transfusion or IV fluids, they must go through a blood warmer - please note this prominently.
- No transfusion needed today; she is hemodynamically stable and producing well.
- CBC in 2 weeks with you, back here in 4 weeks. Rheumatology aware.

Hematology

Exam: no synovitis, no rash.

Ms. Soto (SLE, HAE type I, cold AIHA) is back with her lupus active again: the facial rash has returned after some bright snow-glare days, with mouth sores, aching hands and tiredness for about two weeks.

documents.title: After-hours call: red urine, facial swelling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Sonia texted at 7:20 and I called her back. Since Thursday her urine has been reddish, her face and around her eyes look puffy, and her hands and knees are sore and stiff for an hour or more each morning. Very tired. No throat or tongue swelling, voice normal, breathing fine. No fever she knows of. She says this puffiness feels different from her HAE swelling - soft, both eyes, there on waking.

With SLE this could be nephritis and she needs labs and urine today, which we can't do on a Saturday. Advised ED now; mom will drive. I called the ED to give them a heads-up and flagged that she has HAE type I (procedures/intubation trigger attacks) and cold AIHA (warm any blood products or fluids). Will follow.

events.reason: Hematuria, facial edema, acute kidney injury in SLE

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (1000 mg) by mouth twice daily
40 mg daily, then taper by 5 mg weekly to 20 mg, then by 2.5 mg every 2 weeks to 5 mg daily, per nephrology calendar

results.text: >50/hpf, dysmorphic forms; red cell casts seen

reports.text: Right kidney 11.2 cm, left kidney 11.5 cm. Normal cortical thickness and echogenicity bilaterally. No hydronephrosis, stones or masses. Bladder partially distended, unremarkable. Incidentally, several mobile echogenic shadowing gallstones are seen in a nondistended gallbladder without wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid.
reports.conclusion: Normal-sized kidneys without hydronephrosis; suitable for biopsy. Incidental cholelithiasis.

reports.text: Specimen: left kidney, percutaneous core biopsy (2 cores). Light microscopy: 24 glomeruli, none globally sclerosed; more than half show diffuse global endocapillary hypercellularity with neutrophils and wire-loop deposits. Interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy minimal. Immunofluorescence: full-house pattern (IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q) in mesangial and capillary-wall distribution. Electron microscopy: subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits.
reports.conclusion: Lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS class IV-G (A). Activity index 9/24, chronicity index 1/12.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL - NEPHROLOGY ADMISSION H&P
Date of admission: 02/24/2024

CC: reddish urine, facial puffiness, joint pain, fatigue x 2 days.

HPI: 24-year-old woman with SLE (2021), hereditary angioedema type I on danazol, and cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia, sent in by her PCP. For two days her urine has been red-brown and her face puffy, mostly around the eyes. Fingers and knees are stiff for about an hour each morning. More tired than usual. She mentions sun sensitivity and, when asked, one episode in the past of sharp chest pain on breathing that went away on its own; she never sought care for it. No urticaria. No airway symptoms.

Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg bid, prednisone 5 mg daily, danazol 200 mg tid, folic acid 1 mg, vitamin D3 2000 IU. NKDA.
Family: father HAE; mother SLE and hypothyroidism; maternal aunt RA; paternal grandmother suspected HAE.
Social: veterinary technician, lives on her family's ranch. Never smoker. No alcohol.

Exam: BP 148/94. Afebrile. Mild periorbital edema bilaterally, soft, non-pruritic. Oropharynx normal, no stridor. Small joints of both hands tender without effusion. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No leg edema. No rash.

Data: creatinine 2.0 (normal last November), anti-dsDNA 410 IU/mL, C3 48, C4 4, ESR 56, hemoglobin 10.6. UA protein 2+, blood 3+, dysmorphic RBCs with red cell casts on microscopy; UPCR 2.4 g/g. Urine hCG negative.

Assessment: Active lupus nephritis with acute kidney injury and nephritic sediment.
Plan: renal ultrasound, kidney biopsy once anatomy confirmed; allergy/immunology consulted for peri-procedural HAE prophylaxis; warm all IV fluids/blood (cold AIHA); hold off on immunosuppression changes until tissue diagnosis unless creatinine climbs.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 02/24/2024, discharged 03/05/2024. Service: Nephrology (ICU 02/28-03/01).

Diagnoses:
1. Lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS class IV-G (A), new - kidney biopsy 2/27
2. Laryngeal angioedema attack from hereditary angioedema type I, requiring intubation 2/28-3/1
3. SLE
4. Cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia, stable
5. Cholelithiasis, incidental, asymptomatic

Course:
Renal ultrasound 2/25 showed normal-sized kidneys without hydronephrosis and incidental gallstones. Per allergy/immunology, she received plasma-derived C1 inhibitor 1000 units IV one hour before percutaneous left kidney biopsy on 2/27, which was uncomplicated. Pathology: diffuse proliferative lupus nephritis, class IV-G (A), activity 9/24, chronicity 1/12.
Methylprednisolone 500 mg IV daily 2/27-2/29.
On the morning of 2/28 she developed a hoarse voice and inspiratory stridor. She was given C1 inhibitor 20 units/kg IV, and anesthesia intubated her in the ICU for airway protection. Swelling regressed over 36 hours; leak test passed and she was extubated 3/1 without difficulty. No further swelling during the stay.
Mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily started 2/29. Prednisone 40 mg daily from 3/1 with taper.
Creatinine 2.0 on admission, 1.4 at discharge. Hemoglobin stable at about 10.6, no hemolysis; no transfusion.

Discharge medications:
- Mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg PO twice daily (NEW)
- Prednisone 40 mg PO daily, then down by 5 mg each week to 20 mg, then by 2.5 mg every 2 weeks to 5 mg daily (CHANGED - calendar given)
- Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg PO twice daily
- Danazol 200 mg PO three times daily
- Folic acid 1 mg PO daily
- Cholecalciferol 2000 IU PO daily

Mycophenolate counseling done: risk of birth defects, pregnancy must be avoided; she reports no sexual activity and agrees to two methods if that changes. Pregnancy test negative this admission.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; nephrology clinic 3 weeks with CMP, UA, UPCR, C3; rheumatology and allergy/immunology to be updated.

HPI: 25-year-old with known hereditary angioedema type I on danazol, SLE with class IV nephritis in remission, and cold AIHA. Two days of steadily increasing swelling, first the lips, then the eyelids, hands and feet. No hives or pruritus. documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER, FLAGSTAFF AREA - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/05/2026 16:20. Discharged 03/11/2026. Service: Infectious Disease.

Principal diagnosis: Bubonic plague (Yersinia pestis), left inguinal bubo, with lung involvement.
Other: leukocytosis; thrombocytopenia; SLE with class IV lupus nephritis in remission; hereditary angioedema type I; cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

HPI: 26-year-old woman from Massachusetts working several weeks as a veterinary technician on a cattle ranch here, handling livestock and the ranch's stray cats. Four days of worsening fatigue and chills, a dry cough that turned blood-streaked, and pain in the left groin. A painful sore came up on her ankle shortly after she found and pulled a flea off her sock. Prior hospital care: kidney admission in 2024 and an angioedema ED stay with overnight observation in 2025.
Home meds: mycophenolate 1000 mg bid, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg bid, prednisone 5 mg daily, danazol 200 mg tid, folic acid 1 mg, vitamin D3 2000 IU. NKDA.

Arrival: T 39.2 C (102.6 F), HR 110, RR 30, BP 92/58, SpO2 91% on room air. Ill-appearing and short of breath. 1.5 cm necrotic ulcer on the lateral left ankle; several red macules over both lower legs; tender, fluctuant 4 cm mass in the left inguinal region; crackles at both lung bases.
Labs: WBC 21.4, platelets 92, hemoglobin 11.0, creatinine normal. Portable chest film with bilateral patchy airspace opacities.
Needle aspiration of the inguinal mass: purulent material, Gram stain showing abundant neutrophils with scattered gram-negative rods; culture grew Yersinia pestis, confirmed by the state public health laboratory 3/8.

Course: Droplet precautions for the first 48 hours of therapy. IV ciprofloxacin plus IV doxycycline from the night of admission; IV fluids (warmed, given her cold AIHA) and supplemental oxygen 2 L by nasal cannula; hydrocortisone stress dosing while hypotensive, back to prednisone 5 mg on day 3. Mycophenolate held. Defervesced by day 3, off oxygen day 4, node softening and less tender. Doxycycline stopped and ciprofloxacin changed to oral on day 5. The county health department and state public health were notified on admission and handled contact tracing. No angioedema or hemolysis during the stay.

Discharge medications:
- Ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO twice daily through 3/18/2026 (14 days total) - NEW
- Mycophenolate - HOLD until reviewed by ID at follow-up
- Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg bid, prednisone 5 mg daily, danazol 200 mg tid, folic acid 1 mg, vitamin D3 2000 IU - continue

Follow-up: ID telehealth 3/19; PCP in Massachusetts within a week of return; chest x-ray in 6-8 weeks.
